text:
mike_support: Hey team — ACME (org_1234) is seeing their monthly token bucket show 0 an hour before their expected local reset. They run a long streaming job (2h) that had a bunch of reconnects. Tenant TZ = America/Los_Angeles. Can we check what happened?

emma: Did they give a timeline + sample request ids? Also are they on API or websocket streaming?

mike_support: They sent a couple request ids: req_8a2f, req_8a33. It's websocket streaming. Job started ~2024-11-01T04:45:00Z and ended ~2024-11-01T06:55:00Z. They said UI showed zero ~2024-11-01T06:00:00Z UTC (23:00 PT previous day).

jordan-sre: Quick thoughts — either (1) streaming double-count due to reconnect retries, (2) visible-zero from UI cache TTL mismatch, or (3) our refill scheduler using UTC / tenant TZ mapping edge.

emma: @jordan-sre linked logs? mike, can you paste the small billing trace from the session? A 2–3 line snippet is fine.

mike_support: here's the billing trace excerpt we have from the tenant side:```
2024-11-01T05:58:59.123Z token.consume tenant=org_1234 session=sess_9a token_count=+0 (streaming chunk)
2024-11-01T05:59:00.001Z token.adjust tenant=org_1234 seq=... delta=-1500 reason=streaming-send
2024-11-01T06:00:05.004Z billing.recharge scheduled_at=2024-11-01T07:00:00Z status=pending
```

jordan-sre: That scheduled_at = 07:00:00Z looks odd vs expected PT midnight. For PT midnight the UTC should be 08:00:00Z (depending on DST). Are we sure the tenant TZ mapping stored for org_1234 is America/Los_Angeles? If the mapping was missing system falls back to UTC -> behaves like midnight=00:00Z.

support-ops: I pulled org_1234 from the tenant store: timezone field = "America/Los_Angeles" (v1.2). Recharge scheduler log: `scheduler-run 2024-11-01T07:00:00Z org=org_1234 next_recharge=2024-12-01T07:00:00Z` — looks like the scheduler ran with UTC midnight fallback (07:00Z instead of 08:00Z). Tagging billing-bot to confirm.

billing-bot: Recharge executed: billing.recharge.complete org=org_1234 amount=10000 tokens recharge_ts=2024-11-01T07:00:00Z (event_id=rech_5543)

jordan-sre: That explains server-side timing difference. UI showed zero earlier because their streaming job chewed through the bucket before the (UTC-based) recharge happened. Two contributing factors: (A) scheduler used UTC fallback for this run, (B) streaming session had reconnects that inflated token counts.

emma: Action items: 1) Support to offer customer a temporary top-up to unblock them now. 2) Ops to investigate scheduler timezone fallback bug (why did it fall back though field exists). 3) Engineering investigate streaming token double-count on reconnects.

mike_support: I already offered a +10k token top-up while we investigate; customer accepted.

support-ops: Noted. Created incident INC-2024-7893 to track scheduler TZ fallback. Owner: @jordan-sre. Also created ticket ENG-2024-4411 for streaming accounting edge.

jordan-sre: Quick repro notes for ENG-2024-4411: run a long streaming session, force client reconnects (CTRL-C / reauth), observe token.delta per reconnect. Suspect we double-count buffered chunks when session resumes. Steps: 1) spawn stream w/ small chunk size; 2) kill TCP mid-stream; 3) reconnect and resume; 4) inspect token ledger entries around reconnect event.

emma: For billing ops: please check scheduler code path: if tenant.timezone missing or unparsable we should log and fall back to org-config default (which should be tenant-level), not raw UTC. Also add audit log entry when fallback occurs.

billing-bot: Audit note appended to org_1234: scheduler.fallback=UTC detected at 2024-11-01T06:59:58Z (audit_id=aud_9910)

support-ops: Temporary mitigation guidance for customers: 1) top-up tokens manually via console or billing API; 2) consider switching long-running critical workloads to Dedicated/Reserved (guaranteed capacity) to avoid monthly cutoff issues; 3) for streaming critical flows, enable server-side session resumption mode v2 which deduplicates resumed chunks.

mike_support: Customer confirmed top-up worked and resumed job. They want an explanation email — I'll draft one summarizing scheduler fallback + reconnect accounting, and link to INC-2024-7893 + ENG-2024-4411.

jordan-sre: Follow-up: assigned a short-term patch to scheduler to prefer tenant.timezone atomically and emit a warn if parse fails. ETA: 48h. ENG will also add extra telemetry around streaming reconnect token deltas.

emma: Thanks all. Closing internal thread when ENG & Billing confirm root cause fix deployed. :thumbsup:
